questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I was supposed to go to Asia in the previous spring, but had to cancel due to Coronavirus.
Choosing a destination closer to home seemed to increase the likelihood of a successful exchange.
Also, University of Vienna was one of the few universities that had mathematics courses at a level that i thought would be beneficial.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Possible but not trivial.
It would have been nice to know that the statistics department was at another faculty and thus had a different deadline for course registration.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I recieved an e-mail at before i arrived with information about what to do.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
A physical welcoming event at the local department would have been nice.
I had to figure out the location of all the classrooms on my own.
It would also have been beneficial to have an introduction to the various student activities/networks in the math department.
I kinda felt like I was being left out to dry.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. Applied for StuWo and OEaD and got one.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Completely fine, transport options are good.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Relatively cheap in an otherwise expensive city.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I hardly remember it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I recall getting help from UCPH exchange office and they were quite helpful and flexible.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got in all the classes i wanted - mathematics privilege.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you want to take applied math courses, both statistics, operations research and finance are on the faculty of economics, so be sure to check their course catalogue and registration deadlines.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Some courses had good didactics but some were atrocious.
The biggest sinner was Kinetic Theory Applied to Biology, where we were asked to do assignments throughout the semester with no feedback at all.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Appropriate level for master degree.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The seminars were very good.
UCPH has a severe issue with participation in seminars/exercise classes.
In Vienna all students participated, and the seminars were much more instructive.
In Vienna, the seminars/exercises were taught by faculty, where on UCPH they were taught by other students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Seminar in statistics
Dynamical Systems and Nonlinear Differential Equations (VO and SE)
Biomath seminar
Kinetic Theory Applied to Biology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Biomath Seminar and Seminar in Statistics as well as Dynamical Systems.

questions.answer: Either there were no non-academic activities, or i did not encounter them.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Many small theaters with indie movies.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Many other European cities that are just a couple of hours away by bus.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Most young people speak english just fine.
Tipping and paying in cash is a hassle.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
I only managed to connect with other internationals.
I never had anything more than casual conversation with locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Lack of collective activities made it difficult to make friends.
Having something like student revues or throwing parties to work on something common would have made it much easier to make friends.
At least the danish model of creating engaging student envieronments is based on having the students engage in common activities.
Also, the lack of common areas on campus diminished the opportunity to make friends by working on homework together.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I found that Austrians were good at giving space to each other in a social setting, such that no particular individual would fill the entire room.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go to the ESN events.
Enjoy the parks.
Asian food places are generally the best option if you are vegetarian.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The administration is quite loose, in stark contrast to UCPH.
The professor of a course can sign you up at will, even after the registration deadline, so writing emails solves most issues.
On the other hand, examination formats and dates are not finalized until the semester is almost over, so it's incredibly difficult to plan your return, unless you can accept planning to wait all summer potentially for nothing.
While riding public transport multiple times a day for an entire semester, I did not encounter a ticket control once.
If you wish, you can easily ride without a ticket.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The experience of having to make it more or less on your own in a new envieronment.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Figuring out if a course was challenging because of a different approach to the subject or because it is poorly taught.
Making friends.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: If you are in doubt about whether to go, think about if you really want to go on exchange or you just want to do it because it sounds cool.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
